# Reference: maps, lighting, sound and effects
Load it for: building maps and lobbies, terrain, lighting and atmosphere, particles and beams, sound and music, spawn areas, performance of large worlds

Ask about theme, size and style before building a world: these are taste decisions and cost the most to redo. Part building rules are in `modeling`.

## Layout before detail
- Block out the whole map with plain parts first: walkable paths, landmarks, spawn, boundaries. Check scale against a 5-stud character and check it with `screen_capture`. Detail only after the user is happy with the blockout.
- Paths 8+ studs wide for groups, doorways 5+ wide and 8 tall, steps at most 2 studs high (or use ramps: `Humanoid` climbs slopes up to 89 degrees by default, but 45 feels right).
- Give players a landmark visible from spawn and a clear first direction.
- Keep the playable area bounded: invisible walls (`Transparency = 1`, `CanCollide = true`), or water, cliffs, fog.
- Organise in folders (`workspace.Map.Buildings`, `.Props`, `.Spawns`). Name things. Anchor everything static.

## Terrain
```lua
local terrain = workspace.Terrain
terrain:FillBlock(CFrame.new(0, -8, 0), Vector3.new(512, 16, 512), Enum.Material.Grass)
terrain:FillBall(Vector3.new(40, 6, 20), 18, Enum.Material.Rock)
terrain:FillBlock(CFrame.new(0, -4, 120), Vector3.new(200, 8, 60), Enum.Material.Water)
```
- Terrain is voxels 4 studs wide; sizes below that do nothing useful. Build hills from several overlapping balls and blocks; carve with `Enum.Material.Air`.
- `terrain:Clear()` wipes everything: ask first.
- Mix two or three materials (grass, ground, rock) so large areas do not look flat. Water needs a basin under it.
- For a studded or classic look, use parts for ground instead of terrain; ask which the user wants.

## Lighting
Set these together; one alone rarely looks right.
- `Lighting.Technology`: `Future` for best quality, `ShadowMap` for a cheaper sharp look. Changing it is a Studio property; set it only if asked or if the scene needs real shadows from lights.
- `ClockTime` (14 day, 18 golden hour, 0 night), `GeographicLatitude` for sun angle.
- `Ambient`/`OutdoorAmbient`: not black; soft grey-blue outdoors keeps shadows readable.
- `Brightness` 2 to 3 by day, `EnvironmentDiffuseScale` and `EnvironmentSpecularScale` near 1 for PBR materials.
- Children of Lighting: `Atmosphere` (Density 0.3, Offset, Haze, Color and Decay for depth), `Sky`, `BloomEffect` (subtle: Intensity 0.3 to 0.6), `ColorCorrectionEffect` (small Contrast and Saturation moves, TintColor for mood), `SunRaysEffect`, `DepthOfFieldEffect` (menus and cutscenes only).
- Lights: `PointLight`, `SpotLight`, `SurfaceLight` with `Shadows` on only for a few important ones. Range under 30, warm colours for interiors.
- Keep the user's existing lighting unless asked to change it; say what you changed.

## Particles, beams, trails
- `ParticleEmitter` on a part or Attachment: `Rate`, `Lifetime` (NumberRange), `Speed`, `SpreadAngle`, `Size` and `Transparency` as NumberSequences (fade out at the end), `Color` as ColorSequence, `LightEmission` 1 for glows, `Texture` an asset id. One-shot bursts: `Rate = 0` then `emitter:Emit(20)`.
- `Beam` between two Attachments for lasers, ropes, lightning; `Trail` between two Attachments on a moving part for sword swipes and speed lines.
- Budget: a handful of emitters at modest rates. Hundreds of particles per second per effect will hurt phones.
- Effects for an event (hit, pickup) are created on clients; the server just says where.
- Use real texture ids the user supplies or that already exist in the place; never invent an asset id. With no texture, the default sparkle is acceptable: say so.

## Sound
- `Sound` parented to a part or Attachment is positional (3D); parented to `SoundService` or a GUI is global. Set `RollOffMaxDistance`/`RollOffMinDistance` for 3D sounds.
- Music: one looping `Sound` in `SoundService`, volume 0.2 to 0.4, under a `SoundGroup` so the user can add a mute setting. Crossfade between tracks with tweens on `Volume`.
- UI sounds: play on the client (`SoundService:PlayLocalSound`).
- Asset ids must come from the user or `search_asset`/`insert_asset` when they ask for store audio. Never invent ids; a wrong id is silent and logs an error.

## Spawns and lobbies
- `SpawnLocation` parts: anchored, set `Duration` (forcefield seconds), `Neutral` or `TeamColor`. Several spread out so players do not stack.
- A lobby needs: spawn, where to go (signs or paths), the game's main loop entry (portal, pad, queue), and a place for boards (leaderboards, shop).

## Performance for big maps
- `workspace.StreamingEnabled = true` for large worlds; then client code must `WaitForChild` or use `CollectionService` signals for parts that stream in, and important models can be set `ModelStreamingMode = Persistent`. Turning it on can break scripts that assume everything exists: ask first and check the place's LocalScripts.
- Anchor static parts. `CastShadow = false` on small props and inside buildings. `CanTouch`/`CanQuery = false` on decoration. `CollisionFidelity = Box` on simple meshes.
- Reuse meshes and textures. Avoid thousands of unique unions.
- Part count is not the only cost: transparency layers, lights with shadows, particles and humanoids cost more.
